The canonical PI keeps the id its package, the 11-20 promotion and every interim site build carried (D-0001: a published PI keeps its id); the alias id, which holds all of the PI's identifier anchors (ORCID, DBLP, both collection ids), redirects to it and its anchors move.

Source-proven duplicate (census-name-aliases native_pi_merges, reviewed 2026-11-20). The 11-20 promotion left the alias id active with no PI; it is the later-issued id, so the survivor is the earlier-issued canonical id by R-ID-02 and by D-0001 alike.

anchor_bindings.why: Issued 2026-11-18 from the PI's name+listing-url fallback anchor when the record had no identifier. The 2026-11-20 recovery added the reviewed OpenAlex author id, so a rebuilt record no longer produces the name anchor and would mint a second id. The record still names Zaixi Zhang on the very listing url the issued anchor carries; the new anchor is registered to the issued id.

student_rekeys.why: The record is a 2019 undergraduate research intern on Xiaojuan Ma's student page ("Tim Ta Ying Cheng (Research intern, undergraduate from HKUST, Summer 2019, DPhil@Oxford)"), not the faculty member. A native rebuild keys it by the merged alias PI's collection id (hkust_fac_tim-kwang-ting-cheng), which the registry owns for the faculty id, so it would split and mint a new student id. The 2026-11-20 package carried it re-keyed to its ext: key (R-STU-07); this restores that key before the ID stage so the issued student id 895f96e45082 is reused through its own name+url anchor.
